seed_claims.claim: SEED 8: a fold is a classical shape only if it is larger than its Compton wavelength; the proton is (0.84 fm vs 0.21 fm)
seed_claims.evidence: PDG 2026: r_p/lambda_C = 3.998. Skyrme fold at ANW parameters: M R/hbar c = 2.60 (classical mass) or 2.83 (939 MeV), rotor E_rot/M = 0.085: semiclassical, but only just.

seed_claims.claim: SEED 8: the electron misses the classical-fold condition by at least 1e5
seed_claims.evidence: True but conservative: with LEP's r_e < 1.1e-4 fm (Schael et al. 2013 Eq. 3.9; model dependent, VV contact interaction) lambda_C/R >= 3.51e+06; with SEED's 1e-3 fm 3.86e+05.

seed_claims.claim: SEED 8 / PLAN E7: any soliton whose classical action is S0/g^2 has M R = c0/g^2, so an electron-like fold needs g^2 >> 1
seed_claims.evidence: Theorem for one-scale theories (scaling, sympy-checked for Skyrme); the general criterion is action per light-crossing ~ M R c >> hbar, i.e. R >> lambda_C. Skyrme c0 = 64-120 (radius definition); two-parameter families tested keep c0 >= 47.3 (pion mass to beta = 16, half-baryon radius; 52.1 baryon rms) and hopfion c0 = 341-567. Electron fold needs Skyrme e >= 1.5e+04-2.05e+04 (E_rot/M ~ 7.1e+12) or hopfion 1/kappa4 >= 1.2e+09-2e+09. Semiclassical Skyrme floor M R >= 0.757 hbar/c (0.627 half-baryon radius), 2.66e+06 times above the electron. Not shown for theories with extra dimensionless parameters beyond those tested.

seed_claims.claim: SEED 8: this points toward a strongly coupled fold sector, 'the way baryons are in QCD'
seed_claims.evidence: Strong coupling is necessary, but there the classical fold picture is gone (corrections 1e6-1e13 x the classical mass), so no classical simulation in the seed can model the electron. The QCD baryon is only moderately quantum (M R/hbar c = 2.6-4); the electron needs M R/hbar c <= 2.85e-7.

seed_claims.claim: SEED 8: in weakly coupled theories, folding a few quanta into a pair is exponentially rare
seed_claims.evidence: Demidov-Levkov (read; curve values from the PDF vector paths): P_2 ~ exp(-F/g^2), F = 4.48 at threshold to 3.84 at high energy, i.e. exp(-(0.62-0.72) N_pair). Classical creation needs g^2 N >= 3.98; N_min = n0/g^2 in any one-coupling model by scaling. E1e (phi^4, classical): g^2 N_min <= 2.48 (N = E/m) to 3.38 (N_lin). Unsuppressed (P >= 0.1-0.5) only for g^2 >~ 1.67-5.55 (indicative), where M_S <= 1.87 m.

seed_claims.claim: SEED 8: in nature electron pairs form readily, so the fold sector is strongly coupled
seed_claims.evidence: Electron pairs form readily because QED is weakly coupled and perturbative: Breit-Wheeler peaks at 0.682 pi r_e^2 = 170 mb, power law in alpha. A fold-like exp(-F/g^2) would be 10^-229 (g^2 = alpha) or 10^-18 (g^2 = 4 pi alpha). The inference in SEED does not follow; the seed must produce a pointlike, perturbatively coupled electron out of a strongly coupled fold sector (untested).

seed_claims.claim: SEED 8: why is the vacuum's tension so small (open)
seed_claims.evidence: rho_L = 2.515e-47 GeV^4 = (2.239 meV)^4 (Planck 2018), 1e42 (f_pi^4) to 8.8e122 (M_Pl^4) below natural scales.

seed_claims.claim: SEED 8: can light and the cone be built from the field? (Weinberg-Witten)
seed_claims.evidence: With commitment 1's Lorentz-covariant conserved T^mu nu, a composite massless |h| = 2 graviton is excluded; commitment 5's metric must be fundamental or emergent only via an evasion. A neutral composite photon is not excluded.

seed_claims.claim: SEED 2: one cone, no vacuum dispersion
seed_claims.evidence: Not tested in E7 (E5 checks it by construction).

phi4.DSV_units_note: DSV units lambda = v = 1 (m = sqrt 2) have g^2 = 1, so N*lambda in those units equals g^2 N here
phi4.scaling_argument: Classical solutions depend on (E, N) only through g^2 E and g^2 N (field rescaling phi = phit/g removes g from the field equation); so if classical pair creation exists at all its lower boundary is N_min = n0/g^2 with n0 a pure number of the classical theory, N_min ~ 1/lambda.

weinberg_witten.rule: non-zero forward matrix element needs 2|h| <= j_max; j_max = 1 (J^mu), 2 (T^mu nu)
weinberg_witten.source: Weinberg & Witten, PLB 96, 59 (1980) (original not read); argument read in Porrati arXiv:0804.4672 Sec. 2
statements: A theory with a Lorentz-covariant conserved current J^mu has no massless particle of |h| > 1/2 carrying non-zero charge Q = int J^0.
A theory with a Lorentz-covariant conserved T^mu nu has no massless particle of |h| > 1 (its forward matrix element must be p^mu p^nu/E by the equivalence principle).
Both hold for composite and elementary particles alike; GR and supergravity evade them because the graviton/gravitino T^mu nu is not gauge invariant/Lorentz covariant.
A neutral composite photon (|h| = 1, Q = 0) is not excluded; a composite graviton from a Lorentz-covariant matter sector with covariant conserved T^mu nu is.
